spatial_claims.claim: C is an interior point of segment AB, lying between A and B
ABDE is a square constructed on AB with AB and AE as adjacent sides
AB = AE (sides of the square) and all angles are right angles
AB is decomposed into segments AC and CB with C between A and B
AE is used as the uncut straight line in the application of Proposition 2.1
R(AE,AB) equals the area of square ABDE since AE and AB are adjacent sides

configuration_map: Point C: lies on segment AB between A and B. Used consistently across all steps as the division point of AB into AC and CB. Square ABDE: standard construction on AB via I.46. A is a shared vertex of adjacent sides AB and AE. AE = AB throughout. No auxiliary points beyond the square vertices and the division point C. The proof applies Proposition 2.1 algebraically to the rectangle R(AE,AB) and substitutes AE = AB, requiring no complex spatial arrangement.
pass_reason: The proof's spatial claims are few, simple, and mutually consistent. C lies on AB throughout; the square ABDE is a standard construction; AE = AB is never contradicted. The core reasoning is area-theoretic/algebraic (applying Proposition 2.1 and substituting equal lengths), with no angle decompositions, interior/exterior point arguments, or ray orderings that could generate spatial contradictions.
